Then reason: Before changing orbit, Shenzhou-10 moves on the lower circular orbit 1; after one short-time acceleration, it enters from the inner circular orbit into a transfer orbit that can reach the outer circular orbit 2. This transfer orbit can be regarded as an elliptical orbit, whose perigee radius is approximately equal to the radius of orbit 1, and whose apogee radius reaches the radius of orbit 2, so the semi-major axis of the elliptical orbit is greater than the radius of the original circular orbit 1. According to Kepler's third law T^2 ∝ a^3, the larger the orbital semi-major axis, the larger the operating period. Therefore, the operating period after changing orbit is greater than before changing orbit.
